title: Parables of Jesus
description: Jesus often taught with parables: short stories from everyday life that reveal what God and His kingdom are like.
items: Seed falls on four kinds of soil, like God's word landing in different hearts. Jesus explains it Himself in verses 18-23.
Good and evil grow side by side in the world until the harvest, when God will separate them.
The kingdom of God starts tiny, like the smallest seed, but grows into something great.
A little yeast works through all the dough: God's kingdom quietly changes everything it touches.
The kingdom is worth more than everything we own; finding it brings joy.
A merchant sells all he has for one perfect pearl: nothing compares to knowing God.
A net gathers every kind of fish, and they are sorted at the end, a picture of the final judgment.
Seed grows by itself while the farmer sleeps: God makes His kingdom grow.
A lamp is meant to shine, not be hidden: God's truth is meant to be seen and shared.
Jesus brings something new that cannot be squeezed into old ways.
Building your life on Jesus' words is like building a house on rock.
Someone forgiven much loves much: Jesus' answer to a Pharisee about a woman who honoured Him.
A despised outsider shows what it means to love your neighbour.
Keep on asking, seeking and knocking: God gives good gifts to His children.
A man stores up riches but is not rich toward God.
Be dressed and ready, with lamps burning: the Son of Man will come at an unexpected hour.
A fruitless tree is given one more year: God is patient, but calls for real change.
Choose the humble place, and invite those who cannot repay you.
The invited guests make excuses, so the host welcomes the poor and outcast instead.
Like a builder or a king, think seriously about what following Jesus means.
A shepherd leaves the ninety-nine to find the one that is lost.
A woman searches her whole house for one coin; heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents.
A runaway son comes home, and his father runs to welcome him.
Use money wisely for what lasts: you cannot serve both God and money.
A rich man ignores a poor beggar at his gate, and their places are reversed after death.
Serving God is not a way to earn credit; we simply do our duty.
A widow keeps asking an unjust judge for justice: always pray and don't give up.
The Pharisee and the Tax Collector
God hears the humble prayer: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.
A man forgiven a huge debt refuses to forgive a small one.
Those hired last are paid the same as the first: God's grace is generous.
One son says no but then obeys; the other says yes but doesn't go.
Tenants reject the owner's servants and kill his son: a story about how Jesus would be rejected.
A king's invitation is refused, so it goes out to everyone.
Five are ready when the bridegroom comes and five are not.
Servants are trusted with their master's money: use what God has given you.
Whatever you did for the least of these, you did for me.
Jesus is the good shepherd who knows His sheep and lays down His life for them.

title: Miracles of Jesus
description: Jesus' miracles showed His power over nature, sickness, evil and death, and His compassion for people in need. They point to who He is.
items: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus' first sign revealed His glory.
Jesus heals a boy from far away with a word: "Go, your son will live."
After a night of catching nothing, the nets overflow, and fishermen become disciples.
An Evil Spirit in the Synagogue
Jesus commands an evil spirit to leave, and everyone is amazed at His authority.
Jesus takes her hand, the fever leaves, and she gets up to serve.
Moved with compassion, Jesus touches the untouchable and heals him.
Friends lower him through a roof; Jesus forgives his sins and heals him.
The Man with a Withered Hand
On the Sabbath, Jesus restores a man's hand: it is right to do good.
A Roman officer's great faith: "Just say the word."
Jesus stops a funeral and gives a widow's only son back to her alive.
Even the wind and waves obey Him.
Jesus frees a man from many demons, and he goes home to tell what God has done.
Jairus's Daughter and a Sick Woman
A woman touches His cloak and is healed; a girl is raised to life.
Five loaves and two fish feed a huge crowd, with twelve baskets left over.
Jesus walks on the sea, and Peter walks toward Him.
A non-Jewish mother's persistent faith, and her daughter is set free.
"Ephphatha!" (Be opened!), and the man hears and speaks plainly.
Seven loaves and a few small fish feed another great crowd.
A healing in two stages: first blurry, then perfectly clear.
A Boy with an Evil Spirit
"I believe; help my unbelief!" Jesus heals the boy.
Ill for 38 years, a man is told: "Get up, pick up your mat and walk."
"I was blind, but now I see."
After eighteen years, a woman stands up straight and praises God.
Another Sabbath healing that shows mercy matters more than rules.
Ten are healed, but only one comes back to say thank you.
"I am the resurrection and the life." Lazarus walks out of the tomb.
A beggar calls out, and Jesus gives him his sight.
Peter finds the temple tax in a fish's mouth.
A fruitless fig tree withers: a lesson about faith and prayer.
Even as He is arrested, Jesus heals a servant's ear.
The risen Jesus fills the nets again and cooks breakfast on the beach.
The greatest miracle: He is not here; He has risen!

title: The Ten Commandments
description: God gave His people ten commandments at Mount Sinai (Exodus 20, repeated in Deuteronomy 5). The first four are about loving God, the rest about loving others. Jesus summed them up in two great commandments. (This list follows the common Protestant numbering; Catholic and Lutheran traditions group them slightly differently.)
items: God speaks the commandments to His people at Mount Sinai, after rescuing them from slavery in Egypt.
God alone is God; nothing else should take first place in our lives.
Don't make or worship images: God cannot be reduced to something we make or control.
Don't misuse God's name: speak of Him with reverence and keep your word.
Set apart a day of rest, remembering that God made the world and rested.
Respect and care for your father and mother: the first commandment with a promise.
Life is precious. Jesus taught that even anger and contempt break the heart of this command.
Do not commit adultery. Jesus said faithfulness begins in the heart.
Respect what belongs to others; work honestly and share with those in need.
Do not give false testimony: speak the truth.
Don't long for what belongs to someone else; learn contentment.
Moses reminds the next generation of the commandments before they enter the promised land.
Love God with all your heart, and love your neighbour as yourself: all the commandments hang on these two.

title: The Law of Moses
description: A guided tour of the law God gave through Moses in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy: the covenant, worship, holiness, justice and the great feasts, and how Jesus fulfils it.
items: God reminds Israel how He carried them "on eagles' wings" and invites them to be His treasured people.
Laws against lying, bribery and favouritism, and for kindness to enemies and foreigners.
God asks for a tent where He will live among His people, made from gifts given willingly.
Aaron and his sons are set apart to serve God and represent the people before Him.
The burnt offering: a costly gift that pictured sin being dealt with and a life given wholly to God.
The food laws taught Israel to be set apart: "Be holy, for I am holy."
Once a year the high priest made atonement for all the people's sins.
Leave food for the poor, pay workers fairly, don't hold grudges: love your neighbour as yourself.
God's appointed times: the Sabbath, Passover and Unleavened Bread. Pentecost, Trumpets, Atonement and Tabernacles follow in this chapter.
Every fiftieth year, land returned to its families and slaves went free: a picture of God's restoration.
"The Lord bless you and keep you": the blessing the priests spoke over God's people.
Safe cities where someone who killed by accident could flee for protection: justice tempered with mercy.
"Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one." Love Him with all your heart, and teach your children.
Protect the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, remembering you were once slaves.
Moses sets before the people life and death, blessing and curse: "Choose life."
God promises a new covenant: His law written on hearts, and sins remembered no more.
Jesus came not to abolish the Law and the Prophets but to fulfil them.
The law was a guardian until Christ came; now we are made right with God through faith.

title: Prayers of the Bible
description: Real prayers prayed by real people: for help, forgiveness, wisdom and thanks. Read them, learn from them, and pray them yourself.
items: The prayer Jesus taught His disciples: "Our Father in heaven..."
Abraham boldly asks God to spare the city for the sake of the righteous.
Afraid of meeting Esau, Jacob reminds God of His promises.
After the golden calf, Moses pleads for God's mercy on Israel.
"The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make His face shine on you..."
Hannah prays in deep sorrow for a child, and leaves her burden with God.
"My heart rejoices in the Lord!" Hannah praises God after Samuel is born.
"Who am I, O Lord God?" David marvels at God's promise to him.
Solomon asks for an understanding heart to lead God's people well.
"Hear in heaven, your dwelling place, and forgive."
"Answer me, O Lord, so these people will know that you are God."
Facing a mighty army, Hezekiah spreads the threatening letter before the Lord.
Jabez asks God to bless him and keep him from harm, and God answers.
Nehemiah confesses his people's sins and asks God for favour before the king.
A prayer of trust: God leads, restores and walks with us through the darkest valley.
"Create in me a clean heart, O God." David's prayer after his sin.
God knows us completely and is with us everywhere: "I am fearfully and wonderfully made."
Daniel confesses Israel's sins and pleads for God's mercy, not because of their goodness but His.
From the depths, Jonah cries out and remembers: "Salvation comes from the Lord."
"Though the fig tree does not blossom... yet I will rejoice in the Lord."
"My soul magnifies the Lord." Mary praises God for His mercy.
Zechariah praises God for sending salvation and for his son John.
"Now let your servant depart in peace, for my eyes have seen your salvation."
"God, be merciful to me, a sinner." The humble prayer God hears.
"Not as I will, but as you will." Jesus prays before the cross.
Jesus prays that His followers would be one and know God's love.
On the cross Jesus prays for His enemies and entrusts His spirit to the Father.
Threatened, the believers pray, not for safety, but for courage to keep speaking.
"Lord, do not hold this sin against them."
That you may know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge.
That your love may abound more and more in knowledge and insight.
That you may be filled with the knowledge of God's will and bear fruit.
"To Him who is able to keep you from stumbling..." a closing prayer of praise.
